title: Erdős Problem #980: Sum of Least k-th Power Nonresidues
description: For k ≥ 2, let n_k(p) denote the least k-th power nonresidue modulo prime p. Is it true that Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) ~ c_k · x/log x for some constant c_k > 0? SOLVED: Yes, proved by Erdős (1961) for k=2 and Elliott (1967) for all k ≥ 2.

meta.author: Paul Erdős
meta.assumptions: 15 axiom(s) and 4 sorry(s). See the Lean source for details.

overview.historicalContext: This problem concerns the distribution of k-th power nonresidues among primes. Erdős posed the question in 1961 and proved the quadratic case (k=2) himself, establishing that the sum of least quadratic nonresidues grows like c₂ · x/log x where c₂ = Σ p_j/2^j ≈ 3.67. The general case for all k ≥ 2 was resolved by P.D.T.A. Elliott in 1967. Power residues have been studied since Legendre introduced the Legendre symbol in 1798 to formulate quadratic reciprocity; the distribution of least nonresidues mod primes connects to character sum estimates via the Polya-Vinogradov inequality. Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, the least k-th power nonresidue mod p is O(p^{1/(2k) + ε}), but Elliott established the unconditional asymptotic for the sum over primes.
overview.problemStatement: Let k ≥ 2 and n_k(p) denote the least k-th power nonresidue of prime p. Is it true that Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) ~ c_k · x/log x for some constant c_k > 0?
overview.text: For k ≥ 2, let n_k(p) denote the least k-th power nonresidue modulo prime p. Is it true that Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) ~ c_k · x/log x for some constant c_k > 0? SOLVED: Yes, proved by Erdős (1961) for k=2 and Elliott (1967) for all k ≥ 2.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines k-th power residues and nonresidues, the least nonresidue function n_k(p), and the sum S_k(x) = Σ_{p<x} n_k(p). Erdős's 1961 result for k=2 and Elliott's 1967 generalization are stated as axioms, with the main theorem showing existence of the positive constant c_k for all k ≥ 2.
keyInsights: The least k-th power nonresidue n_k(p) is well-defined for primes p > k
The constant c₂ = Σ_{j≥1} p_j/2^j where p_j is the j-th prime, converging to approximately 3.67
The average value of n_k(p) over primes p < x is roughly c_k · log x
Vinogradov's bound shows n(p) = O(p^{1/(4√e)+ε}) unconditionally
Under GRH, the least quadratic nonresidue satisfies n(p) = O((log p)²)
prerequisites: Analytic number theory: the prime number theorem, prime counting function, and summation over primes
Power residues and the Legendre symbol: k-th power residues modulo primes and character sums
Asymptotic analysis: asymptotic equivalence, big-O notation, and convergent series over primes
Character sum estimates: the Polya-Vinogradov inequality and bounds on least nonresidues

sections.title: Power Residues and Nonresidues
sections.summary: Defines IsPowerResidue, IsPowerNonresidue, and leastPowerNonresidue (using Nat.find). States Vinogradov's bound n(p) = O(p^{1/(4√e)+ε}) and the GRH conditional bound n(p) = O((log p)²).

sections.title: The Sum Function S_k(x)
sections.summary: Defines sumLeastNonresidues S_k(x) = Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) using Finset.range with primality filter. Axiomatizes nonnegativity.

sections.title: The Constants c_k
sections.summary: Defines c_2 = Σ p_j/2^j (≈ 3.67) as a tprime series, axiomatizes c_2_positive and c_2_approx (3.5 < c₂ < 4). Defines general c_k with positivity axiom for k ≥ 2.

sections.title: Erdős's Result (1961)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Erdős's 1961 result: Σ_{p<x} n_2(p) ~ c₂ · x/log x in both absolute error and ratio convergence forms.

sections.title: Elliott's Generalization (1967)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Elliott's 1967 generalization to all k ≥ 2. States erdos_980_solution (the main theorem), average interpretation, special cases (n₂(p) = 2 for p ≡ ±3 mod 8), Pólya-Vinogradov connection, and the summary theorem.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #980 is SOLVED. The conjecture is true: for all k ≥ 2, the sum Σ_{p<x} n_k(p) ~ c_k · x/log x with c_k > 0. Erdős proved the k=2 case in 1961 with the explicit constant c₂ = Σ p_j/2^j. Elliott completed the solution in 1967 by proving the general case for all k ≥ 2.
conclusion.implications: The result shows that on average, the least k-th power nonresidue among primes p < x grows like c_k · log x. This connects to character sum estimates and the distribution of power residue symbols.
openQuestions: What are the exact values of c_k for k > 2? Can they be expressed as explicit prime-weighted series like c₂?
Can the error term in the asymptotic Σ n_k(p) = c_k · x/log x + E(x) be improved? What is the best possible bound on E(x)?
How does the distribution of individual n_k(p) values compare to the average? What fraction of primes have n_k(p) = 2?
Is there an analog for composite moduli, or does the result fundamentally require primality?

crossReferences.description: The prime number theorem π(x) ~ x/log x is foundational to interpreting the asymptotic Σ n_k(p) ~ c_k · x/log x.
